### Nixpkgs version

- Stable (26.05)

### Describe the bug

Upgrading to NixOS 26.05 broke SSH authentication using a key stored in a PIV smartcard (a Yubikey in my case).

`ssh-keygen` works and returns the public key associated with my Yubikey PIV applet using OpenSC or Yubico library:
```
$ ssh-keygen -D /nix/store/ak8bafnmvadbfc4k2i2v08bfx6p1p0r5-opensc-0.27.1/lib/opensc-pkcs11.so
ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 AAAA<redacted> PIV AUTH pubkey
$ ssh-keygen -D /nix/store/dajaf335xdgp4x38wl7i38f09b7kbrpq-yubico-piv-tool-2.7.3/lib/libykcs11.so
ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 AAAA<redacted> Public key for PIV Authentication
ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 AAAA<redacted> Public key for Retired Key 1
ssh-rsa AAAA<redacted> Public key for PIV Attestation
```

### Steps to reproduce

This requires a PIV smartcard containing a SSH key to reproduce.

Connecting to a OpenSSH server configured to accept the public key:
```
$ ssh -v -I /nix/store/ak8bafnmvadbfc4k2i2v08bfx6p1p0r5-opensc-0.27.1/lib/opensc-pkcs11.so server
```

### Expected behaviour

A PIN prompt should appear and then wait for a physical button press.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Relevant log output

```console
$ ssh -v -I /nix/store/ak8bafnmvadbfc4k2i2v08bfx6p1p0r5-opensc-0.27.1/lib/opensc-pkcs11.so server

debug1: pkcs11_record_key: Already seen this key at provider /nix/store/ak8bafnmvadbfc4k2i2v08bfx6p1p0r5-opensc-0.27.1/lib/opensc-pkcs11.so slot 0 keyid 01

### Nixpkgs version

- Stable (26.05)

### Describe the bug

wpa_supplicant service fails in attempt to change ownership recursively in `/etc/wpa_supplicant` .

Relevant code

https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/b7d6bfe6d1a56d46c9ac7ec8e2f07a65186f8034/nixos/modules/services/networking/wpa_supplicant.nix#L122-L127

https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/b7d6bfe6d1a56d46c9ac7ec8e2f07a65186f8034/nixos/modules/services/networking/wpa_supplicant.nix#L82-L86

### Steps to reproduce

Configure `networking.wireless` with non-declarative config.
Before upgrading to 26.05 per [release notes](https://nixos.org/manual/nixos/stable/release-notes#sec-release-26.05) I moved my existing `/etc/wpa_supplicant.conf` into `/etc/wpa_supplicant` (created along the way) and added

```nix
networking.wireless.extraConfigFiles = [ "/etc/wpa_supplicant/home.conf" ]; # TODO: ensure wpa_supplicant can read it
```

Try switch

### Expected behaviour

I was expecting it to fail as I still had to do `chown` with new user `wpa_supplicant` that only added after in 26.05.  
I was planning to do chown and restart service.
But it failed even before starting.

### Screenshots

```

- [CVE-2026-48525](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-48525) - [Nixpkgs security tracker issue](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/issues/NIXPKGS-2026-1803) - affected package maintainers: cc @prikhi ## Description PyJWT is a JSON Web Token implementation in Python. From 2.8.0 to 2.12.1, when verifying detached JWS tokens using the unencoded-payload option ("b64": false, RFC 7797), PyJWT performs Base64URL decoding of the compact-serialization payload segment before enforcing the detached-payload rules. For b64=false, PyJWT later discards that decoded payload and replaces it with the caller-provided detached_payload. In practice, this turns the middle segment into an attacker-controlled “work amplifier”: a remote client can supply an arbitrarily large Base64URL payload segment that forces CPU work + memory allocations even if the signature is invalid. This creates an unauthenticated DoS vector against any endpoint that verifies detached JWS using PyJWT. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.13.0. ## References - [https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/security/advisories/GHSA-w7vc-732c-9m39](https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/security/advisories/GHSA-w7vc-732c-9m39) (`x_refsource_CONFIRM`, `exploit`)

## Description

CryptX versions before 0.088_001 for Perl have a stack buffer overflow in four AEAD decrypt_verify helpers.

The gcm_decrypt_verify, ccm_decrypt_verify, chacha20poly1305_decrypt_verify and eax_decrypt_verify XS routines copied the caller-supplied authentication tag into a fixed 144-byte stack buffer (MAXBLOCKSIZE) without checking the supplied length. A longer tag overwrites the stack past the buffer. Version 0.088 added the clamp to gcm_decrypt_verify, and 0.088_001 added it to the other three.

Any caller of an affected helper that forwards an attacker-controlled tag longer than the buffer can trigger the overflow.


## References

- https://github.com/DCIT/perl-CryptX/commit/57e69e541b0718ca8724c2f61514322a2d859bc1.patch (`patch`)
- https://github.com/DCIT/perl-CryptX/commit/7e56347d420aaf43b2ee1586f4a230492ccf1642.patch (`patch`)
- https://metacpan.org/release/MIK/CryptX-0.088_001 (`release-notes`)
- http://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/05/28/10


<details>
<summary>Affected packages</summary>

- `perlPackages.CryptX` (0.088@nixos-25.11, 0.088@nixos-unstable)
- `perl5Packages.CryptX` (0.088@nixos-unstable)
- `perl538Packages.CryptX` (0.088@nixos-25.11)
- `perl540Packages.CryptX` (0.088@nixos-25.11)
</details>

Prior to 2.13.0, PyJWKClient passes its uri argument directly to urllib.request.urlopen() which uses Python stdlib's default OpenerDirector registering HTTPHandler, HTTPSHandler, FTPHandler, FileHandler, and DataHandler. There is currently no documented option to restrict which schemes PyJWKClient will fetch. If an application's jku URL ingestion path accepts attacker-influenced URLs (e.g., from JWT header, configuration file, OAuth flow parameter), the attacker can cause PyJWKClient to read arbitrary local files via file:// (SSRF on local filesystem), cause PyJWKClient to attempt FTP / data-URI fetches (broader SSRF surface), or forge tokens that PyJWT verifies as valid. The library does not directly return non-HTTP(S) URI contents to the attacker; the chained "plant a JWKS to forge tokens" scenario described in the original report requires additional application-layer flaws (attacker write access to a filesystem path, untrusted jku derivation) that this fix does not address. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.13.0. ## References - [https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/security/advisories/GHSA-993g-76c3-p5m4](https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/security/advisories/GHSA-993g-76c3-p5m4) (`x_refsource_CONFIRM`)

From 2.9.0 to 2.12.1, there is a verifier-side algorithm allow-list bypass when jwt.decode() or jwt.decode_complete() are called with a PyJWK key. The token header alg is checked against the caller-supplied algorithms allow-list, but signature verification is performed with the algorithm bound to the PyJWK object instead of the header algorithm. An attacker who controls a registered JWK/JWKS private key can sign with a disallowed algorithm, advertise an allowed algorithm in the JWT header, and still be accepted. The issue affects the documented PyJWKClient.get_signing_key_from_jwt(...) flow. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.13.0. ## References - [https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/security/advisories/GHSA-jq35-7prp-9v3f](https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/security/advisories/GHSA-jq35-7prp-9v3f) (`x_refsource_CONFIRM`, `exploit`)

- [CVE-2026-8594](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-8594)
- [Nixpkgs security tracker issue](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/issues/NIXPKGS-2026-1781)

## Description

Text::LineFold versions through 2019.001 for Perl duplicate the output based on the number of special break characters.

Text::LineFold splits the input string by specific line break characters (such as VT, FF and others) into segments, but applies the break function to the entire string, not just the segment.

A side effect of this is that the full input can be duplicated for each segment.  Besides being incorrect, this can lead to unexpected resource consumption and possible denial of service.

Note that Text::LineFold is part of the Unicode-LineBreak distribution, which may have a higher version number than the module.


## References

### Nixpkgs version

- Stable (26.05)

### Describe the bug

`nix-serve` (when run manually outside the NixOS module) by default listens on both IPv4 and IPv6. However the NixOS option `services.nix-serve.bindAddress` defaults to `0.0.0.0`, which has the effect of disabling IPv6.

Setting `services.nix-serve.bindAddress` to the empty string resolves the issue, but I'm not sure if this would be considered a safe change to the default.

### Steps to reproduce

Set `services.nix-serve.enable = true;` in NixOS and try to connect to it over IPv6.

You can also see the behavior in the logs of `nix-serve`.

```bash
nix-serve --listen :5001
```
shows
```text
2026/05/31-10:45:47 Starman::Server (type Net::Server::PreFork) starting! pid(168190)
Resolved [*]:50001 to [::]:50001, IPv6
Not including resolved host [0.0.0.0] IPv4 because it will be handled by [::] IPv6
Binding to TCP port 50001 on host :: with IPv6
Setting gid to "100 100 1 57 62 67 100 302"
```

but

```bash
nix-serve --listen 0.0.0.0:5001
```
shows
```text
2026/05/31-10:46:06 Starman::Server (type Net::Server::PreFork) starting! pid(168484)
Binding to TCP port 5001 on host 0.0.0.0 with IPv4
Setting gid to "100 100 1 57 62 67 100 302"
```

### Expected behaviour

IPv6 should be supported by default.

payload.author: rcambrj
payload.body:
### Describe the problem

NixOS 26.05 makes systemd stage 1 / initrd the default, and the release notes document several non-automatically-detectable incompatibilities. However, I could not find a migration note for configurations that rely on `/dev/root`.

With the old scripted stage 1, `/dev/root` was created by the stage 1 init script from the `root=` kernel command line. With systemd stage 1, this compatibility path is not available in the same way. Machines with configurations that mount `/dev/root` directly **can stop booting** after switching to systemd stage 1.

This seems worth documenting because nixpkgs itself appears to have needed this migration for installation media. In `nixos/modules/installer/cd-dvd/iso-image.nix`, the `/iso` filesystem now uses `/dev/disk/by-label/${config.isoImage.volumeID}` when `config.boot.initrd.systemd.enable` is true, and only uses `/dev/root` for the non-systemd initrd path:

https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/c16db5827622adb804336437d250df477a30994a/nixos/modules/installer/cd-dvd/iso-image.nix#L795-L798

The nearby comment also says that `/dev/root` is created in the stage 1 init script:

https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/c16db5827622adb804336437d250df477a30994a/nixos/modules/installer/cd-dvd/iso-image.nix#L791-L793

The scripted stage 1 init script still contains the compatibility symlink creation:

https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/c16db5827622adb804336437d250df477a30994a/nixos/modules/system/boot/stage-1-init.sh#L230-L243

There is also a previous issue showing this exact failure mode for ISO images with systemd stage 1:

https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/327187

In my own configuration, the required migration was to replace `/dev/root` with a stable device path, for example `/dev/disk/by-label/nixos`:

https://github.com/rcambrj/dotfiles/commit/d082630edee0a0feb4deb72433212a4390ecfad0#diff-edf34d58eccea1d69562cd98e09950b05719e48898d94348dfc9c189f3fa063eL46-R49 (please forgive my noisy commit)

The current 26.05 release notes mention that systemd stage 1 is now default, but the listed caveats do not mention `/dev/root`:

https://nixos.org/manual/nixos/unstable/release-notes#sec-release-26.05

Expected documentation:

The 26.05 release notes, or the systemd stage-1 migration documentation, should explicitly mention that configurations should not rely on `/dev/root` when using systemd stage 1, and should instead use a stable device reference such as:

* `/dev/disk/by-label/...`
* `/dev/disk/by-uuid/...`
* the appropriate `/dev/mapper/...` path
* another stable device path appropriate for the system

### Proposed solution

```markdown
Configurations should not rely on `/dev/root` when using systemd stage 1. In the old scripted stage 1, `/dev/root` was a symlink created by the init script from the `root=` kernel command line. With systemd stage 1, this symlink is not provided in the same way. If your configuration mounts `/dev/root` directly, for example in `fileSystems.*.device` or other initrd/early-boot mounts, replace it with a stable device path such as `/dev/disk/by-label/...`, `/dev/disk/by-uuid/...`, or the appropriate `/dev/mapper/...` path.
```

### Notify maintainers

cc @yayayayaka @jopejoe1 @NotAShelf @bryanhonof since this concerns a potentially boot-breaking 26.05 migration note.

### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.11)

### Describe the bug

`wrapFirefox` fails on Darwin when wrapping a Firefox-based browser whose macOS app bundle path contains spaces and parentheses

I hit this while building `zen-beta` from `0xc000022070/zen-browser-flake` on `aarch64-darwin`.

The wrapped app bundle is named: `Zen Browser (Beta).app`

With nixpkgs e9a7635a57597d9754eccebdfc7045e6c8600e6b, the generated build script includes an unquoted path: `touch $out/${libDir}/is-packaged-app`

On Darwin, libDir expands to a path like: `Applications/Zen Browser (Beta).app/Contents/Resources`

The resulting shell command fails because `(Beta)` is parsed as shell syntax rather than as part of a path.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use nixpkgs `e9a7635a57597d9754eccebdfc7045e6c8600e6b` on `aarch64-darwin`.
2. Build a Darwin package using `wrapFirefox` where `browser.applicationName` contains spaces and parentheses.
3. For example, build `zen-beta 1.20.1b` from `0xc000022070/zen-browser-flake`.
4. Observe that the generated wrapper derivation fails during the build script evaluation.

### Expected behaviour

`wrapFirefox` should quote generated paths so Darwin app bundle names containing spaces, parentheses, or other shell-sensitive characters build correctly.

For example, this generated command:

```sh
touch $out/${libDir}/is-packaged-app
```

should likely be:
```sh
touch "$out/${libDir}/is-packaged-app"
```

### Nixpkgs version

- Stable (26.05)

### Describe the bug

The migartion to gcc 15 broke dwmblocks, when conf is set, then it does not compile and fails with error
`cp: target 'gcc15': No such file or directory`

### Steps to reproduce

1. add dwmblocks with conf overridden to packages

### Expected behaviour

I was able to determine the cause of this bug.
It is the following line in dwmblocks derivation:
```nix
lib.optionalString (conf != null) "cp ${configFile} blocks.def.h"
    + ''
      # gcc15
      substituteInPlace dwmblocks.c \
        --replace-fail 'void termhandler()' 'void termhandler(int signum)'
    '';
```
Due to there not being a newline or any other whitespace after blocks.def.h, bash sees blocks.def.h# gcc15 and doesn't treat it as a comment.
The simplest fix would be to either add a newline after blocks.def.h or remove the # gcc15 comment
e.g.
```nix
lib.optionalString (conf != null) "cp ${configFile} blocks.def.h\n"
    + ''
      # gcc15
      substituteInPlace dwmblocks.c \
        --replace-fail 'void termhandler()' 'void termhandler(int signum)'
    '';
```

payload.body:
### Nixpkgs version

- Stable (26.05)

### Describe the bug

Hyprland [uses a wrapper](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/9ff29b46ff3d87c940380a8e2cb3d39d87081c9c/nixos/modules/programs/wayland/hyprland.nix#L93) (added in #507419) to grant the cap_sys_nice capability. However, the wrappers framework drops TZDIR (defined in [unsecvars.h](https://sourceware.org/git/?p=glibc.git;a=blob;f=sysdeps/generic/unsecvars.h;h=33755179f348dd3263c5469f7f0320bbbbea60e5;hb=refs/heads/master#l38) in glibc), which causes some applications started by Hyprland to be unable to determine the timezone. Notably, this affects all flatpak applications, as flatpak relies on TZDIR for its time zone setting. E.g. Chromium started in flatpak will use UTC time in websites as it thinks the system time is the default UTC.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `echo $TZDIR` to confirm it is set
2. Run `Hyprland` to open Hyprland
3. Inside Hyprland, open a terminal and run `echo $TZDIR` and see it is not set.
4. Alternatively, run `sudo cat /proc/$(pgrep Hyprland)/environ | tr '\0' '\n' | grep TZ` to see that the Hyprland process does not have TZDIR set.
5. (optional/downstream) Run e.g. `flatpak run --command=date org.freedesktop.Platform/x86_64/25.08` and see that it displays UTC time, whereas a normal `date` does not unless your system time is set to UTC

### Expected behaviour

While it is unclear where TZDIR should be set, out-of-the-box Hyprland+flatpak should be able to load the system time zone.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Relevant log output

```console

```

### Additional context

Workaround: add `hl.env("TZDIR", "/etc/zoneinfo")` to your hyprland.lua, or `env = TZDIR,/etc/zoneinfo` if you're still on the old config format.

### Describe the bug

The adguard module seems to override all http settings. I noticed this when I upgraded my server to nixos 26.05 and adguard refused to start. http:

payload.body:
### Nixpkgs version

- Stable (26.05)

### Describe the bug

# Description

`horizon-client` crashes immediately when launched from a GNOME desktop session via its `.desktop` file, whether triggered by clicking a `vmware-view://` protocol link or by launching the application directly from GNOME. The same binary works correctly when invoked from a terminal.

The crash does not produce a visible error; the application silently exits. The failure is only visible in the journal.

# Environment
 
- NixOS: 26.05
- Package: omnissa-horizon-client 2512
- Desktop environment: GNOME (GDM, Wayland session)
- GPU: NVIDIA (relevant to session LD_LIBRARY_PATH contents)


### Steps to reproduce

1. Install omnissa-horizon-client on NixOS 26.05 with a GNOME desktop
2. Log into a GNOME session
3. Either:
  - Navigate to a page that redirects to a `vmware-view://` URL and let Firefox open the handler, or
  - Run `gio open "vmware-view://test"` from a terminal, or
  - Double-click the Omnissa Horizon Client application in the GNOME app launcher
4. Observe the application fails to open

Running horizon-client directly from a terminal works correctly.

### Expected behaviour

The browser should correctly open vmware-view:// protocol links.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Relevant log output

```console
horizon-client.desktop[742030]: /usr/lib/omnissa/horizon/bin/horizon-client:
/lib/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_ABI_DT_X86_64_PLT' not found
(required by /nix/store/57iz36553175g3178pvxjij8z5rcsd4n-glibc-2.42-61/lib/libmvec.so.1)
```

### Additional context

# Root Cause

The GNOME session populates `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` with Nix store library paths (for GTK, GPU drivers, etc.), including `/nix/store/57iz36553175g3178pvxjij8z5rcsd4n-glibc-2.42-61/lib`. This leaks into the FHS chroot created by `buildFHSEnv`.

Inside the chroot, the dynamic linker resolves `libmvec.so.1` from the Nix store glibc 2.42 path (via the inherited `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`) rather than from the chroot's `/lib`. However, `libmvec.so.1` from glibc 2.42 requires the versioned symbol `GLIBC_ABI_DT_X86_64_PLT` from `libc.so.6`, which was introduced in `glibc 2.42`. The chroot's `/lib/libc.so.6` comes from an earlier glibc version and does not export this symbol, causing the linker to abort.

From a terminal, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` is not set (or does not include the glibc 2.42 path), so the chroot resolves all glibc components consistently from its own `/lib`, and the binary launches successfully.

# Workaround

Override the system-level horizon-client.desktop with a user-level entry that clears `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` before entering the FHS chroot:

```
[Desktop Entry]
Name=Omnissa Horizon Client
Exec=env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH /nix/store/…-omnissa-horizon-client-2512/bin/horizon-client %u
Type=Application
MimeType=x-scheme-handler/vmware-view;x-scheme-handler/horizon-client;
```

# AI Disclosure

Claude Code running locally did guide me to this solution and provided details for the writeup. I can verify the workaround does restore horizon functionality.

payload.author: IzuCha
payload.body:
In `nix repl`:

```nix
nix-repl> :lf github:nixos/nixpkgs?ref=2f6693b8e559782230e116f5262c7527a85259f4
nix-repl> f = x: x
nix-repl> g = lib.mirrorFunctionArgs f f
```

Both functions act the same when called:

```nix
nix-repl> f "test"
"test"

nix-repl> g "test"
"test"
```

But `f` is a lambda and `g` is a [functor](https://noogle.dev/md/tutorials/functors/):

```nix
nix-repl> f
«lambda @ «string»:1:2»

nix-repl> g
{
  __functionArgs = { ... };
  __functor = «lambda __functor @ /nix/store/0g1phlns5rn4nc8xixjvxhk4xpcz60hn-source/lib/trivial.nix:1183:19»;
}
```

Which causes `lib.typeOf` to return `"set"` instead of `"lambda"` for `g`:

```nix
nix-repl> lib.typeOf f
"lambda"

nix-repl> lib.typeOf g
"set"
```

**This can lead to hard to catch bugs.** For example, I had a function that worked as expected when called with a lambda, but it didn't work properly when called with a functor because it handled attribute sets differently. This is difficult to catch because lambdas and functors act similarly in most situations.

I don't know what the fix should be, but it should probably be at least documented.

---

Relevant behavior from other functions:
* `builtins.isFunction` returns `true` for lambdas and `false` for functors.
* `lib.isAttrs` returns `false` for lambdas and `true` for functors (it might be a good idea for this to be documented as well).
* `lib.isFunction` returns `true` for both, because it handles functors.
https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/2f6693b8e559782230e116f5262c7527a85259f4/lib/trivial.nix#L1127-L1131

### Nixpkgs version

### Describe the bug

Relying on libvirt's dnsmasq for DHCP on a system with `networking.stevenblack.enable = true` leaves guests unable to acquire IP addresses.

### Steps to reproduce

1. set `networking.stevenblack.enable = true`
2. start or restart libvirt network (e.g.  `sudo virsh net start default`)

### Expected behaviour

The entry should be omitted from the generated hosts file.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Relevant log output

```console

### Nixpkgs version

- Beta (26.05)

### Describe the bug

Apparently the order of some settings (like `local_name`) matters in `dovecot.conf`,
but they're generated in lexicographic order.

### Steps to reproduce

When using a config like:
```nix
{
  services.dovecot2.settings =
    {
      ssl_server_cert_file = "/var/lib/acme/example.org/fullchain.pem";
      ssl_server_key_file = "/var/lib/acme/example.org/key.pem";
      "local_name mail.example.edu" = {
        ssl_server_cert_file = "/var/lib/acme/example.edu/fullchain.pem";
        ssl_server_key_file = "/var/lib/acme/example.edu/key.pem";
      };
    };
}
```
generating a `dovecot.conf` like:
```
[…]
local_name mail.example.edu {
  ssl_server_cert_file = /var/lib/acme/example.edu/fullchain.pem
  ssl_server_key_file = /var/lib/acme/example.edu/key.pem
}
[…]
ssl_server_cert_file = /var/lib/acme/example.org/fullchain.pem
ssl_server_key_file = /var/lib/acme/example.org/key.pem
[…]
```


### Expected behaviour

No warnings. Eg. by having `local_name` treated differently to be generated at the end of `dovecot.conf`.

### Screenshots

_No response_

- [CVE-2026-48959](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-48959)
- [Nixpkgs security tracker issue](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/issues/NIXPKGS-2026-1766)

## Description

IO::Uncompress::Unzip versions before 2.220 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via per-byte read loop in fastForward.

fastForward() compares length $offset (the digit count of the offset, 1 to 19) against the chunk size $c instead of $offset itself, so $c shrinks from 16 KiB to 1-19 bytes per iteration.

Extracting a named entry from an attacker supplied zip via IO::Uncompress::Unzip->new($zip, Name => $target) drives a per-byte read loop scaling with the entry's compressed size, up to the non-Zip64 4 GiB cap.


## References

- https://github.com/pmqs/IO-Compress/commit/68db44076f4c1a86a2ffe53a958eac6cabaf72e2.patch (`patch`)
- https://metacpan.org/release/PMQS/IO-Compress-2.220/changes (`release-notes`)

- [CVE-2026-48961](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-48961)
- [Nixpkgs security tracker issue](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/issues/NIXPKGS-2026-1762)

## Description

IO::Compress versions from 2.207 before 2.220 for Perl ship a zipdetails CLI tool that crashes with undefined subroutine on Info-ZIP Unix Extra Field with 8-byte UID or GID.

When decode_ux() in bin/zipdetails handles an Info-ZIP Unix Extra Field (tag 0x7875) with UID Size or GID Size set to 8, causing zipdetails to decode an 8-byte UID or GID value, it dispatches through decodeLitteEndian(), which calls a misnamed helper unpackValueQ. The actual function defined in the same file is unpackValue_Q (with underscore); the call raises 'Undefined subroutine &main::unpackValueQ' and the script exits with status 255.

Library callers of IO::Compress and IO::Uncompress are not affected; the defect is in the bundled CLI tool.

In 0.9.15 and earlier, LibVNCClient's Tight encoding decoder uses fixed-size 2048-pixel scratch buffers for the Gradient filter, but it does not reject Tight rectangles whose width is larger than 2048 pixels. ## Description

IO::Uncompress::Unzip versions before 2.215 for Perl propagate uncaught exception when parsing zip header with malformed DOS date.

_dosToUnixTime() decodes the local-file-header last-modification date field and calls Time::Local::timelocal() without an eval guard. A header whose date field decodes to an out-of-range month, day, or hour causes timelocal() to die.

The exception propagates out of IO::Uncompress::Unzip->new($file) where callers expect undef plus $UnzipError.

From 1.0.0 to before 1.0.2, an logic error causes anchor programs to accept any program id when requiring the system program id, causing false assumptions resulting in potential arbitrary cpi in programs that invoke system program instructions. In the TryFrom<&'a AccountInfo<'a>> implementation for Program<'a, T>, the id of T is compared with Pubkey::default() to check whether anchor should allow any executable account, or a specific account, because when no T is supplied, T defaults to (), which implements Id::id() by returning Pubkey::default(). This results in T = () and T = System (which has Pubkey::default() as the id) having the same behavior, both allow any executable account. Programs built with anchor assume that the anchor runtime verifies passed in programs of type Program<'a, System> are in fact the system program. This false assumption can lead to arbitrary CPI or payment bypassing when programs try making CPI calls to the system program using the passed in system program due to the fact that the attacker can pass in any program instead of the system program. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.0.2. ## References - [https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/security/advisories/GHSA-c6rc-8jpp-2fgc](https://github.com/otter-sec/anchor/security/advisories/GHSA-c6rc-8jpp-2fgc) (`x_refsource_CONFIRM`)

Prior to 2.13.0, ParameterAnalysis in pkg/scanning/parameterAnalysis.go runs two sequential worker stages that both write to the same results channel. The channel is correctly closed after the first stage completes (close(results) at line 438), but the second stage — which processes POST-body parameters (dp) — is then launched with the same already-closed channel as its output. When a scanned parameter is reflected, processParams executes results <- paramResult on the closed channel, triggering a Go runtime panic that crashes the entire dalfox process. In server mode, the crash is remotely triggerable by any unauthenticated caller who can reach the REST API, because the default configuration has no API key and the second stage activates whenever options.Data != "" (i.e., the attacker supplies the data field) and the target reflects at least one parameter. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.13.0. ## References - [https://github.com/hahwul/dalfox/security/advisories/GHSA-2g4x-fq3j-cgq4](https://github.com/hahwul/dalfox/security/advisories/GHSA-2g4x-fq3j-cgq4) (`x_refsource_CONFIRM`) - [https://github.com/hahwul/dalfox/releases/tag/v2.13.0](https://github.com/hahwul/dalfox/releases/tag/v2.13.0) (`x_refsource_MISC`)

payload.body:
### Nixpkgs version

- 25.11

### Describe the bug

I recently did an update to my NixOS and after that all XWayland programs showed low FPS and tearing. It seems that this regression was introduced by 6.12.91, I did not have any problems with 6.12.90.

I tested with the open NVIDIA drivers, versions 595.71.05 and 580.142 and the version of the NVIDIA driver did not seem to have any effect. The issue also seemed to persist after switching to the closed drivers. I'm using RTX 4090 as my dGPU.

Here are the results of all my tests:
```
kernel   | nvidia     | works?
6.18.33  | 595.71.05  | NO: tearing/stuttering
6.12.90  | 580.142    | YES (nixpkgs rev d233902339c02a9c334e7e593de68855ad26c4cb)
6.18.33  | 580.142    | NO: tearing/stuttering
6.12.91  | 595.71.05  | NO: tearing/stuttering
6.12.91  | 580.142    | NO: tearing/stuttering
```

I ran `vkcube` via XWayland to test for issues with `env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY vkcube`. For all the versions that didn’t work, I saw horizontal tears and the framerate did not go above 29, while with the good version I got no tearing and 60 FPS. I did not notice any issues when running `vkcube` on Wayland natively.

After some digging around, I found out that `nvidia-x11-595.71.05` no longer installs the necessary EGL json files in `/run/opengl-driver/share/egl/egl_external_platform.d/`, which causes XWayland programs to pick my iGPU as the rendering device instead of the dGPU. I had to copy these JSON files from an older nvidia derivation over to a new directory and then point the `__EGL_EXTERNAL_PLATFORM_CONFIG_DIRS` environment variable to that directory before launching Sway. With that workaround I managed to get XWayland programs running with normal performance and no tearing.

I assume these JSON files should be installed automatically, but currently they are not being installed.

### Steps to reproduce

On `64c08a7ca051951c8eae34e3e3cb1e202fe36786`, install kernel version 6.18.33 and 595.71.05 (or any other combo from the table). Launch sway, then run `env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY vkcube`. Observe that the program picks the iGPU as the rendering device.

### Expected behaviour

I would expect XWayland programs to use my dGPU, not the integrated GPU.

## Problem

cargoHash produces different hashes on each build for restate package.

## Error

```
error: hash mismatch in fixed-output derivation '/nix/store/jzaw2z3hf0cvdhxwwwf6j90gwg7qvsa5-restate-1.6.2-vendor-staging.drv':
         specified: sha256-LfLqScEqBJK9s+xRg2Ah1OnBEDQjXQ9LgJGusmxEDfk=
            got:    sha256-VrxoxygLkw+77ORgFnFmIVY4CRVgWevWkiFcYxiPkpw=
```

## Cause

restate has git dependencies with submodules. nix-prefetch-git --fetch-submodules fetches them non-deterministically, causing hash mismatches.

## Git Dependencies

- base62-2.2.3
- raft-0.7.0, raft-proto-0.7.0
- rdkafka-0.38.0, rdkafka-sys-4.9.0+2.12.1
- restate-web-ui-0.1.49
- rust-librocksdb-sys-0.41.0+10.9.1, rust-rocksdb-0.45.0
- sasl2-sys-0.1.22+2.1.28

https://github.com/johnfanv2/LenovoLegionLinux/compare/f559df04cc0705b2b181dfd0404110a4d1d6e2a9...7c19579d13ce686cf1e237699b9a78e80d03c977

### Additional context

• This update fixes Lenovo Legion Linux functionality on Linux 7.x kernels.

  Locally tested on NixOS unstable with:

  - Kernel: `7.0.9-zen2`
  - Package override: `lenovo-legion` / `lenovo-legion-module`
  - Upstream commit: `7c19579d13ce686cf1e237699b9a78e80d03c977`

  After the update, the following work again on my Lenovo Legion laptop:

  - `legion_cli --donotexpecthwmon hybrid-mode-status`
  - fan / hybrid-mode controls through Lenovo Legion Linux
  - platform profile integration through `power-profiles-daemon`

  Before this update, the older Nixpkgs package did not work correctly on Linux 7.x because the
  kernel-side device layout changed. The newer upstream code handles this by using the new Linux
  7 path while keeping older kernel paths available.

  The upstream source appears intended to remain backward compatible: it has explicit kernel-
  version branches for `< 7.0`, `< 6.14`, and `< 6.13`. I have only runtime-tested this exact
  bump on Linux `7.0.9-zen2`, so I recommend backtesting the module against currently supported
  Nixpkgs kernels, especially 6.12 LTS and any 6.18/6.19-era kernels present in the channel.

  If the update regresses older supported kernels, it may be worth either:

  - keeping the package version conditional on kernel version, or
  - applying the Linux 7 compatibility changes as a smaller patch on top of the current Nixpkgs
  version.

  Packaging note: this upstream revision already contains a literal package version in
  `setup.cfg`, so the existing `_VERSION` substitution used by the current Nixpkgs expression
  may need to be removed or adjusted.

### Nixpkgs version

- Stable (25.11)

### Describe the bug

The version of nixpkgs currently in 25.11 has a deprecation that throws an error:  'wmii_hg' has been renamed to/replaced by 'wmii' in aliases.nix.

However the version of nixos/modules/services/x11/window-managers/wmii.nix currently in 25.11 directly references 'wmii_hg' itself, thus even if all references to 'wmii_hg' are replaced with references to 'wmii' in configuration.nix, nixos-rebuild will *still* fail on any configuration that tries to use wmii as the window manager.

This seems to be caused by out-of-sync backports:  the version of nixos/modules/services/x11/window-managers/wmii.nix in master no longer references 'wmii_hg' but it seems this change was not backported to 25.11 when the updated aliases.nix from nixpkgs was backported/pushed to the 25.11 channel.

### Steps to reproduce

Attempt nixos-rebuild with any configuration.nix that has services.xserver.windowManager.wmii-enable set to true while on the 25.11 channel.

### Expected behaviour

Rebuilding should not fail with an error when 'wmii_hg' is no longer referenced in configuration.nix (or alternatively 'wmii_hg' should continue to be allowed in 25.11 and this change held back until 26.05).

### Nixpkgs version

- Stable (25.11)

### Describe the bug


Bluetooth stopped working after `linuxPackages_6_12` was updated to kernel `6.12.90` in nixpkgs. It worked correctly on `6.12.87`.

The adapter is detected but fails to initialize with:
```
Bluetooth: hci0: Failed to send wmt func ctrl (-22)
Bluetooth: hci0: HCI Enhanced Setup Synchronous Connection command is advertised, but not supported.
```

As a result, `bluetoothctl show` reports "No default controller available" and blueman cannot find the adapter.

## Hardware

- **Adapter**: IMC Networks Wireless_Device (`13d3:3563`) — MediaTek MT7921 chipset
- **Driver**: `btusb` / `btmtk`
- **Firmware**: `BT_RAM_CODE_MT7961_1_2_hdr.bin` (present in `linux-firmware`)

```
$ lsusb | grep -i bluetooth
Bus 003 Device 003: ID 13d3:3563 IMC Networks Wireless_Device
```


## Workaround

Pin `boot.kernelPackages` to `linuxPackages_6_12` from nixpkgs commit `d7a713c` (which provides `6.12.87`):

```nix
nixpkgs-kernel.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/d7a713c";
boot.kernelPackages = inputs.nixpkgs-kernel.legacyPackages.x86_64-linux.linuxPackages_6_12;
```



### Steps to reproduce

1. Run NixOS with `linuxPackages_6_12` on nixpkgs `25.11` (commit `b77b3de` or later)

payload.body:
Rust package builds using `fetchCargoVendor` have started failing intermittently with HTTP 403 responses when downloading crate tarballs from `https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/<name>/<version>/download`. The failures are not caused by any recent change in nixpkgs, they're triggered server-side by crates.io, which has begun blocklisting specific `python-requests/<version>` User-Agent strings.

This was fixed for `fetchCargoDeps` in https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/512735, but `importCargoLock` is a separate fetcher that is still affected by this issue. Currently, this affects 106 packages out of all 2759 Rust packages (3.84%)

See also the upstream issue https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io/issues/13482

CC @emilazy @andresilva

payload.author: alain-san
payload.body:
### Describe the bug

The Immich plugin subsystem (introduced around Immich 2.5/2.7) stores the **absolute path** to a plugin's WebAssembly file in the database, in the `plugin.wasmPath` column. On NixOS this path points into the Nix store of the Immich package that was running *at install time* (e.g. `/nix/store/<hash>-immich-2.5.6/...`).

After upgrading the `services.immich.package` (or after the store path otherwise changes), Immich keeps reading the **stale** `wasmPath` from the DB instead of the current package's path. Once the old store path is garbage-collected, the core plugin fails to load on every startup:

```
ERROR [Api:PluginService] Failed to load plugin immich-core:
ERROR [Api:PluginService] Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open
'/nix/store/8scas56xy9wfxlw55lq3g1kzdlpjayqn-immich-2.5.6/lib/node_modules/immich/build/corePlugin/dist/plugin.wasm'
```

The server still starts and core functionality (upload, gallery, search, faces) works, but the `immich-core` plugin — which provides workflow **filters** (by filename, file type, person) and **actions** (archive, favorite, add to album) — is unavailable.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy `services.immich.enable = true` on a given nixpkgs revision (Immich populates the `plugin` table with `wasmPath` = the current store path).
2. Bump nixpkgs so `pkgs.immich` resolves to a newer version (here `immich-2.5.6` → `immich-2.7.5`).
3. `nixos-rebuild switch` (or `boot` + reboot) and run `nix-collect-garbage` so the old store path is removed.
4. Restart `immich-server` and inspect the logs.

The plugin's `.wasm` file **does exist** in the new package — the manifest even references it relatively:

```
/nix/store/<new-hash>-immich-2.7.5/lib/node_modules/immich/build/corePlugin/dist/plugin.wasm
```
```json
// .../corePlugin/manifest.json
{ "name": "immich-core", "version": "2.0.1", "wasm": { "path": "dist/plugin.wasm" }, ... }
```

But the DB still holds the old absolute path:

```sql
SELECT name, version, "wasmPath", "updatedAt" FROM plugin;
-- name      | immich-core
-- version   | 2.0.1
-- wasmPath  | /nix/store/8scas56xy9wfxlw55lq3g1kzdlpjayqn-immich-2.5.6/.../dist/plugin.wasm
-- updatedAt | 2026-02-20   (install time, never refreshed on upgrade)
```

### Expected behavior

The bundled `immich-core` plugin should load regardless of how many times the package's store path changes. Either:
- the NixOS module / Immich should refresh `plugin.wasmPath` to the running package's path on startup, or
- the path stored should be stable across rebuilds (not a raw, GC-able store path).

### Workaround

There is **no UI/API way** to refresh it — the plugin API in 2.7.5 exposes only read routes (`GET /api/plugins`, `/api/plugins/:id`, `/api/plugins/triggers`). The only manual fix is an `UPDATE plugin SET "wasmPath" = ...` to the current store path, which must be redone on every upgrade and is fragile — so it's not a real fix.

### Notes

- No environment variable controls the plugin path; `immich-server` resolves and persists it internally.
- Impact is silent: the server starts fine, so users may not notice the core plugin is disabled until they try to use workflow filters/actions.

### Metadata

- nixpkgs revision: `64c08a7ca051951c8eae34e3e3cb1e202fe36786`
- NixOS: `26.05.20260523.64c08a7 (Yarara)`
- Immich: `2.5.6` → `2.7.5`, plugin `immich-core` `2.0.1`
- Module: `nixos/modules/services/web-apps/immich.nix`

cc @dotlambda @jvanbruegge @Scrumplex @titaniumtown @diogotcorreia

- [CVE-2026-42496](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-42496)
- [Nixpkgs security tracker issue](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/issues/NIXPKGS-2026-1729)

## Description

Archive::Tar versions before 3.08 for Perl extract symlinks with attacker controlled targets outside the extraction directory.

_make_special_file() passes the tar header's linkname to symlink() without validating it against absolute paths or .. segments. The secure-extract mode check that guards regular file extraction does not cover the symlink target.

A subsequent open through the extracted name reads or writes the attacker chosen path.


## References

- https://github.com/jib/archive-tar-new/commit/17c873492a05eddc0de18c1485e0b2cccd5a9158.patch (`patch`)
- https://metacpan.org/release/BINGOS/Archive-Tar-3.08/changes (`release-notes`)
- https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-42497 (`related`)

- [CVE-2026-9538](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-9538)
- [Nixpkgs security tracker issue](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/issues/NIXPKGS-2026-1724)

## Description

Archive::Tar versions before 3.10 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via attacker controlled entry size field in tar header.

_read_tar() reads each entry's payload with $handle->read($$data, $block), where $block is derived from the entry's 12-byte size field in the tar header with no upper bound on that value.

A crafted header declaring a multi-gigabyte size causes Perl to allocate a scalar of that size.


## References

- https://github.com/jib/archive-tar-new/commit/f9af01426038e29d9578825a0cd3626946ab08c7.patch (`patch`)
- https://metacpan.org/release/BINGOS/Archive-Tar-3.10/changes (`release-notes`)
- http://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/05/26/4


<details>
<summary>Affected packages</summary>

Prior to 6.13.0, DeviceResource.uploadImage authorizes the target device only through Condition.Permission(User.class, getUserId(), Device.class) and then immediately streams the uploaded body into mediaManager.createFileStream(...). Unlike the generic mutation path in BaseObjectResource.update and the explicit device mutation handler updateAccumulators, this route never invokes permissionsService.checkEdit(getUserId(), Device.class, false, false). The skipped guard is exactly where Traccar enforces readonly and deviceReadonly restrictions for non-admin users. An unauthorized user can replace a device’s stored image file under the server media directory. This allows modification of UI-visible device media and any downstream workflows that rely on the persisted image, despite other device update paths correctly rejecting the same identity. This vulnerability is fixed in 6.13.0. ## References - [https://github.com/traccar/traccar/security/advisories/GHSA-33v4-5x2g-7mjm](https://github.com/traccar/traccar/security/advisories/GHSA-33v4-5x2g-7mjm) (`x_refsource_CONFIRM`, `exploit`)

payload.author: zh4ngx
payload.body:
Beeper Desktop currently needs Nixpkgs to patch minified JS to prevent the app from downloading or prompting for self-updates.

Nixpkgs installs Beeper from the Linux AppImage, so updates should come through Nix rather than the app replacing itself. We currently pass `--no-update`, patch `auto_update_disabled`, patch `executeDownload`, and hide the About-page update status. This has worked, but it is brittle because the relevant code is minified. It already broke once and produced invalid JS:

https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/484180

@slice, you helped us reason through the logging issue in #486164. Do you know if there is a supported way to disable Beeper Desktop self-updates for distro packages?

The ideal fix would be one stable interface, for example:

- a CLI flag like `--disable-updates`
- an env var like `BEEPER_DISABLE_UPDATES=1`
- a config key that disables both automatic and user-triggered update checks/downloads
- making the existing `--no-update` flag fully disable the updater on Linux

If none of those exists today, is there a less brittle file or setting we should patch than `resources/app/build/main/main-entry-*.mjs`?

Prior context: #401086, #401415, #484180, #486164.
payload.title: beeper: need supported way to disable self-updates

payload.author: qweered
payload.body:
For context, `builtins.derivation` handles derivation attrs quite differently depending on whether `__structuredAttrs` is enabled.

When disabled, attrs are generally injected via environment variables unless `passAsFile` is used.

When enabled, most attrs are serialized into `NIX_ATTRS_JSON_FILE` and `NIX_ATTRS_SH_FILE`; they don't become environment variables. See [docs](https://nix.dev/manual/nix/2.34/store/derivation/#structured-attrs).

`NIX_ATTRS_SH_FILE` declares shell variable, _not_ exported environment variables. However, stdenv _does_ export variables from the `env` attrset as environment variables [here](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/507c78db9f50b400f77556cc72b2c9095e5eb0fa/pkgs/stdenv/generic/setup.sh#L571-L577).

`NIX_ATTRS_SH_FILE` does not export environment variables; it initializes shell variables. Bash shell variables do not have a size limit.

Further, `ARG_MAX` / `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` issues arise when spawning a new process and passing large argv/env payloads. They do not apply to calling a shell builtin within the current shell process; `printf` is a bash builtin.

So if the replacement were `/usr/bin/printf` or another external command, then yes, this could run into exec-size limits. But `printf %s "$foo"` itself should not.

---

Aside: we should probably have a "passing large values into derivations" section in the nixpkgs manual and/or wiki and/or nix.dev. I'd be happy to review something along those lines.

_Originally posted by @MattSturgeon in https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/205690#issuecomment-4546367743_
payload.title: Document how to pass large values into derivations

payload.author: ShamrockLee
payload.body:
## Description

The automatically-packaged GNOME extensions currently use the "file ID" as `version`. Such file ID is a serial number https://extensions.gnome.org use to identify extension files of each version of an extension.

However, such ID is less informative and intuitive to users and extension developers compared to the three-number "shell version" most extension project uses to tag their releases. Such "shell version" is also the version presented to users who manually download extension files from `extensions.gnome.org`.

One use case is to inspect whether the diff of a commit has been included in the current extension package.

Take `gnomeExtensions.paperwm` as an example.

The upstream commit https://github.com/paperwm/PaperWM/pull/1010/commits/d9a4e5fced0bd5d0f708f924103d957d86a9661b fixes the extension PaperWM's behaviour on touchscreens.
The GitHub commit description page shows that the tag `v48.0.3` comes after such upstream commit, indicating that it has been released since version `48.0.3`.

For users who would like to know if such change is included in the Nixpkgs package `gnomeExtensions.paperwm`, it's natural that they can evaluate `pkgs.gnomeExtensions.paperwm.version`, only to find the file ID `"148"`. It is hart to find out which extension version corresponds to the file ID 148, and which file ID correspond to the version `48.0.3`. The current way to determine that would be manually downloading the PaperWM extension file with extension version 48.0.3 from https://extensions.gnome.org/extension/6099/paperwm/ and see the file ID `142` in the file name `paperwmpaperwm.github.com.v142.shell-extension.zip`.

Could we somehow fetch and expose both "file ID" and "shell version"?

## Unresolved question

Do we want to switch the `version` attribute value to "shell version" instead of "file ID"? That would make our version consistent with other package providers on Repology: E.g.: https://repology.org/project/gnome%3Apaperwm/versions
## Maintainers

- @honnip
- @jtojnar
- @NixOS/gnome

### Nixpkgs version

- Beta (26.05)

### Describe the bug

Upgrading libqmi from 1.36.0 to 1.38.0 adds **+121 MiB** to the NixOS system closure.

```
$ nix store diff-closures /nix/store/rga6ni3v8yi4m0nlc5pvwidhjpfk5hsw-nixos-system-foo-25.11.20260522.b77b3de /nix/store/lgjc9dbh6znrlh3i2xmym2nj764rw151-nixos-system-foo-26.05.20260524.705e992 | grep libqmi
libqmi: 1.36.0 → 1.38.0, +124031.1 KiB
```

libqmi 1.38.0 now ships a large `share/doc/` directory (72 MB) that was not present in 1.36.0:

```
1.36.0:
  8.0K  share/bash-completion
   16K  share/man

1.38.0:
  8.0K  share/bash-completion
   72M  share/doc          ← new, unbundled
   16K  share/man
```

The nixpkgs expression does not split documentation into a separate `doc` output, so every system that depends on libqmi pays this cost in its closure.


### Steps to reproduce

```
$ nix build github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-26.05#libqmi
$ du -sh result/share/*
8.0K	result/share/bash-completion
72M	result/share/doc
16K	result/share/man
```

### Expected behaviour

The closure size of libqmi 1.38.0 should be close to 1.36.0

### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.11)

### Describe the bug

After updating `flake.lock` to nixpkgs `29916453413845e54a65b8a1cf996842300cd299` (2026-05-23), sway 1.11 crashes with `SIGABRT` within minutes of any login, dumping the user back to the TTY login. A fresh login immediately starts a new sway which then crashes again the same way, in a tight loop.

The only version change in sway's dependency closure between the working and broken generations is **libdrm 2.4.131 → 2.4.133**. sway 1.11, wlroots 0.19.3, mesa-libgbm 26.0.3, seatd 0.9.3 and libinput 1.31.1 are unchanged in version — only rebuilt against the new libdrm.

The crash signature is identical on every occurrence and matches the wlroots libseat-during-teardown bug class (see related issues below).


### Steps to reproduce

1. NixOS 26.05 (unstable) on AMD GPU, sway as compositor, seatd (libseat) backend.
2. Update `flake.lock` to nixpkgs rev `29916453413845e54a65b8a1cf996842300cd299` and rebuild.
3. Log in to sway. Use the desktop normally (open a terminal, switch workspaces).
4. Within ~1–2 minutes sway aborts and the wayland session terminates.

### Expected behaviour

sway runs stably (as it did on the prior generation with libdrm 2.4.131).

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Relevant log output

```console
#0  __pthread_kill_implementation        (libc.so.6)
#1  raise                                (libc.so.6)
#2  abort                                (libc.so.6)
#3  __assert_fail_base.cold              (libc.so.6)
#4  wlr_backend_finish.cold              (libwlroots-0.19.so)
#5  multi_backend_destroy                (libwlroots-0.19.so)
#6  wl_signal_emit_mutable               (libwayland-server.so.0)
#7  wlr_backend_finish                   (libwlroots-0.19.so)
#8  backend_destroy.part.0               (libwlroots-0.19.so)
#9  wl_signal_emit_mutable               (libwayland-server.so.0)
#10 wlr_session_destroy                  (libwlroots-0.19.so)
#11 libseat_event                        (libwlroots-0.19.so)
```

### Additional context

Reproduces at least 5 times in ~6 minutes in the journal; identical trace every time.

## Diagnosis
Comparison of `nix-store -q --requisites` on the working (gen 493) and broken (gen 494) `sway-1.11` derivations:

| Package | Before (working) | After (broken) |
|---|---|---|
| sway | 1.11 | 1.11 |
| wlroots | 0.19.3 | 0.19.3 |
| mesa-libgbm | 26.0.3 | 26.0.3 |
| seatd | 0.9.3 | 0.9.3 |
| libinput | 1.31.1 | 1.31.1 |
| **libdrm** | **2.4.131** | **2.4.133** |

libdrm is the only version change. Everything else has a new store hash only because it was rebuilt against the new libdrm.

The stack trace points at the known wlroots/libseat teardown-race bug class — see related issues. The libdrm bump appears to change DRM device-release timing enough to trigger the abort path reliably.


## Workaround

`nixos-rebuild switch --rollback` to the previous generation (libdrm 2.4.131) makes sway stable again.

### System metadata

```
nixos-version: 26.05.20260515.d233902 (Yarara)  [previous generation, working]
                26.05.20260523.64c08a7         [broken generation]
nixpkgs rev (working): da5ad661ba4e5ef59ba743f0d112cbc30e474f32
nixpkgs rev (broken):  29916453413845e54a65b8a1cf996842300cd299
kernel: 7.0.10
GPU: AMD (PCI vendor 0x1002)
sway: 1.11
wlroots: 0.19.3
libdrm: 2.4.133 (broken) / 2.4.131 (working)
session backend: libseat → seatd 0.9.3
```

payload.author: 5UP4F15H
payload.body:
## Description

`nixos/modules/system/boot/luksroot.nix` reads LUKS passphrases through shell variable expansion, which silently truncates binary data at the first null byte (`\x00`). This violates the `cryptsetup` contract that [key files can contain arbitrary binary data](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/cryptsetup.8.html):

> A passphrase stored in a file is called a key file. The only difference between a passphrase and a key file is that a key file can contain binary data.

## The problem

In `do_open_passphrase()` ([line 205](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/system/boot/luksroot.nix#L205)):

```bash
passphrase=$(cat /crypt-ramfs/passphrase)
```

And then ([line 235](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/system/boot/luksroot.nix#L235)):

```bash
echo "$passphrase" | ${csopen}
```

While `cat` itself is binary-safe, `$()` (command substitution) stores the result in a **shell variable**, which is a C string — null-terminated by definition. POSIX shells cannot hold `\x00` in variables. Any bytes from the first null onward are silently discarded.

The result: if a LUKS key file written to `/crypt-ramfs/passphrase` contains any null bytes, the key presented to `cryptsetup` is truncated and decryption silently fails. The system hangs at boot waiting for the root device with no error message.

## Impact

For a randomly generated N-byte key, the probability of at least one null byte is:

```
P = 1 - (255/256)^N
```

| Key size | Probability of silent boot failure |
|----------|-------------------------------|
| 32 bytes | 11.8% |
| 64 bytes | 22.1% |
| 256 bytes | 63.3% |

This manifests as an intermittent boot hang that is extremely difficult to diagnose. Any setup that writes a machine-generated binary key to `/crypt-ramfs/passphrase` via `preOpenCommands` (e.g. retrieving a key from a remote KMS or TPM at boot) will hit this non-deterministically.

## Introduced by

Commit [`a9d69a74d6e`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/commit/a9d69a74d6edb6bcca29b1189d4bc3b203ecaf25) (2017-09-15) — *"nixos: initrd/luks: change passphrases handling"* — which introduced the `/crypt-ramfs` mechanism to support `reusePassphrases`.

## Suggested fix

When the passphrase originates from a file (written to `/crypt-ramfs/passphrase` by `preOpenCommands` or similar), pass it directly as a key file rather than routing through a shell variable:

```bash
# Instead of:
passphrase=$(cat /crypt-ramfs/passphrase)
echo "$passphrase" | ${csopen}

# Use:
${csopen} --key-file=/crypt-ramfs/passphrase
```

The `reusePassphrases` feature can still work — the file persists in ramfs between devices. Only the shell-variable intermediary needs to be removed for the file-sourced path.

For interactively-typed passphrases (which cannot contain null bytes by nature of terminal input), the current behavior is acceptable.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Generate a random key: `dd if=/dev/urandom bs=32 count=1 of=/tmp/luks-key`
2. Verify it contains a null byte: `grep -cP '\x00' /tmp/luks-key` (must be > 0)
3. Create a LUKS volume with that key as key-file
4. Configure NixOS with `preOpenCommands` that copies the key to `/crypt-ramfs/passphrase`
5. Reboot — the system will hang every time

To see the 12% rate: repeat steps 1-5 with a fresh random key each time.
Alternatively, any key containing a `\x00` byte demonstrates the bug deterministically.

## Metadata

- **NixOS version:** affects all versions since 2017
- **Architecture:** all

payload.body:
### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.11)

### Describe the bug

Hardware-accelerated screensharing in Discord Canary currently breaks for me when using the NVIDIA driver package from `nixpkgs-unstable`, but works when building the same or newer upstream NVIDIA driver versions with the older stable nixpkgs NVIDIA packaging recipe.

This is **not** Discord's native Linux encoder path. Discord Canary is patched locally using the same general approach as:

https://github.com/relativemodder/discord-linux-vulkan-video-patcher

The patch enables Discord's Linux Vulkan/NVENC-related experiments in `discord_voice/index.js`.

I understand that this is not an officially supported Discord feature. However, the same patched Discord Canary package and the same upstream NVIDIA driver version behave differently depending only on the nixpkgs NVIDIA packaging recipe used to build the driver. That makes this look like a possible nixpkgs-side regression in the NVIDIA packaging refactor.

## System

- NixOS
- Wayland / Hyprland
- `hardware.nvidia.open = true`
- Kernel from `nixpkgs-unstable`: `linuxPackages_latest`
- Current kernel tested: `7.0.9`
- Discord Canary from `pkgs-unstable.discord-canary`
- Discord Canary patched declaratively in the NixOS configuration
- Vencord enabled through the nixpkgs Discord Canary override

## Tested combinations

| Driver | nixpkgs NVIDIA recipe | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `580.142` | stable NVIDIA recipe | works |
| `580.142` / `legacy_580` | unstable NVIDIA recipe | broken |
| `595.71.05` / `production` | unstable NVIDIA recipe | broken |
| `595.71.05` via stable `nvidiaPackages.mkDriver` | stable NVIDIA recipe | works |

The important data point is `580.142`: it uses the same upstream NVIDIA driver version and hashes in both stable and unstable, but only the unstable recipe breaks screensharing.

This suggests that the upstream NVIDIA driver version alone does not explain the regression.

## Discord Canary patching

Discord Canary is patched declaratively during the Nix build instead of mutating an installed Discord directory manually.

The package is based on `pkgs-unstable.discord-canary` with Vencord enabled:

```nix
discordCanaryBase = pkgs-unstable.discord-canary.override {
  withVencord = true;
};
```

Then `discord_voice/index.js` is modified during `postInstall`:

```nix
discord-canary = discordCanaryBase.overrideAttrs (oldAttrs: {
  nativeBuildInputs = (oldAttrs.nativeBuildInputs or [ ]) ++ [ pkgs.python3 ];

  postInstall = (oldAttrs.postInstall or "") + ''
    index_js="$out/opt/DiscordCanary/resources/discord_voice/index.js"

    python3 - "$index_js" <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re
import sys

path = Path(sys.argv[1])
text = path.read_text()

text = re.sub(r'"vaapi"\s*,\s*', '', text)

if '"linux-nvenc"' not in text:
    text = text.replace(
        '"linux-v4l2",',
        '"linux-v4l2","linux-nvenc","useCaptureDeviceForEncode",',
        1,
    )

if '"linux-vulkan"' not in text:
    text = re.sub(
        r'("linux-v4l2"\s*,\s*"linux-nvenc"\s*,\s*"useCaptureDeviceForEncode"\s*,)',
        r'\1"linux-vulkan",',
        text,
        count=1,
    )

path.write_text(text)
PY
  '';
});
```

The wrapper also exposes the OpenGL driver libraries to Discord Canary:

```nix
wrapProgram "$out/opt/DiscordCanary/DiscordCanary" \
  --prefix LD_LIBRARY_PATH : /run/opengl-driver/lib
```

The same patched Discord Canary package was used across the working and broken tests. The variable changed in the successful workaround was only the NVIDIA nixpkgs recipe used to build the driver.

## Runtime symptoms

With the working NVIDIA driver recipe, Discord Canary logs show the stream using the NVIDIA encoder successfully, for example:

```text
codec: H265 (nvidia: cuda)
```

The stream starts normally, with a valid resolution and frame rate.

With the broken unstable NVIDIA recipe, Discord still appears to detect the encoder path, but the stream never starts producing frames. The logs show symptoms like:

`

### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.11)

### Describe the bug

Systemd requires the presence of an `/etc/machine-id` file in order to properly initialize various services, such as tmpfiles, logging, and networking. If this file is not present, systemd will print:

```
System cannot boot: Missing /etc/machine-id and /etc/ is read-only.
Booting up is supported only when:
1) /etc/machine-id exists and is populated.
2) /etc/machine-id exists and is empty.
3) /etc/machine-id is missing and /etc/ is writable.
```

which aptly describes the options. Note that boot does not stop or fail when this is printed, but subsequent systemd components will probably fail.

### Steps to reproduce

A minimal reproduction of this issue can be found in the following expression:

```nix
pkgs.testers.nixosTest {
  name = "immutable-etc-test";

  nodes.machine =
    { pkgs, modulesPath, ... }:
    {
      imports = [ "${modulesPath}/profiles/image-based-appliance.nix" ];
      system.etc.overlay.enable = true;
      system.etc.overlay.mutable = false;
      systemd.sysusers.enable = true;
    };

  testScript = ''
    machine.wait_for_unit("multi-user.target")
  '';
}
```

via `nix build -L` or similar. The relevant part of the logs from doing so is attached in this issue. You can also evaluate an existing nixos test with this issue present via `nix build nixpkgs#nixosTests.activation-etc-overlay-immutable -L`, in which several failures occur from the lack of `/etc/machine-id` and the test hangs.

### Expected behaviour

The simplest expected behavior here is to have `system.etc.overlay.mutable = false;` implicitly set a blank `/etc/machine-id` (`environment.etc."machine-id".text = lib.mkDefault "";` or similar). As systemd says in its error message, this would allow systemd to bind mount over it with a newly generated machine-id. The prior issue #268995 might be relevant.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Relevant log output

```console
vm-test-run-immutable-etc-test> machine # [    5.024258] systemd[1]: systemd 260.1 running in system mode (+PAM +AUDIT -SELINUX +APPARMOR +IMA +IPE +SMACK +SECCOMP +GCRYPT -GNUTLS +OPENSSL +ACL +BLKID +CURL +ELFUTILS +FIDO2 +IDN2 +KMOD +LIBCRYPTSETUP +LIBCRYPTSETUP_PLUGINS +LIBFDISK +PCRE2 +PWQUALITY +P11KIT +QRENCODE +TPM2 +BZIP2 +LZ4 +XZ +ZLIB +ZSTD +BPF_FRAMEWORK -BTF -XKBCOMMON +UTMP +LIBARCHIVE)
vm-test-run-immutable-etc-test> machine # [    5.029326] systemd[1]: Detected virtualization kvm.

vm-test-run-immutable-etc-test> machine # [    5.031348] systemd[1]: Detected first boot.
vm-test-run-immutable-etc-test> machine # [    5.036993] systemd[1]: System cannot boot: Missing /etc/machine-id and /etc/ is read-only.

```

### Additional context

It seems like this issue should have been caught by tests, such as `activation-etc-overlay-immutable` failing when they hang for a long time and have all their individual targets fail. I am going to look into this further, as I am not currently very familiar with the nixos testing and CI infrastructure.

payload.body: There are a number of packages where enabling an optional feature requires bringing in a nontrivial library, such as `gpsd` or `avahi` ([Example 1](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/f5e0041fc9b35ee7e086fa79baf388afba48d7a1/pkgs/by-name/di/direwolf/package.nix#L1-L22); [Example 2](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/ab1436b980e30e768eb8fc386c978ee49e7c9247/pkgs/by-name/mo/monado/package.nix#L1-L63)). For things like CUDA or ROCm, following the `config` value is obviously the right way to go, but for the vast majority of packages right now, it's up to individual package maintainers to determine which dependencies to have installed by default and/or which combinations to expose as variants. However, this leaves users with no good model for what features they can expect when installing a package from nixpkgs, and can lead to disagreements between package maintainers that lead to PRs stalling (e.g. https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/498631/changes#r2915406526). Thoughts?

payload.body:
### Nixpkgs version

- nixos-unstable, after #522661 (`opencloud: 6.2.0 -> 7.0`, merged 2026-05-21).
- Reproduced on `26.05.20260523.2991645`.

### Describe the bug

OpenCloud 7.0 made the `sharing` service's `service_account` block mandatory (upstream opencloud-eu/opencloud#2735). Existing NixOS installs that were initialised on 6.x via `services.opencloud.enable = true` ship a `/etc/opencloud/opencloud.yaml` that populates `service_account: {id, secret}` for every service *except* `sharing:`. After the daily flake.lock sync pulled in 7.0, the unit crash-loops:

```
The service account id has not been configured for sharing. Make sure your /etc/opencloud
config contains the proper values (e.g. by using 'opencloud init --diff' and applying the
patch or setting a value manually in the config/corresponding environment variable).
```

→ 5 quick restarts → `start-limit-hit` → `opencloud.service` ends up in `failed`. Same crash is reported widely in other distros' issue trackers (opencloud-eu/opencloud#2811, truenas/apps#5027, community-scripts/ProxmoxVE#14650).

The version bump PR (#522661) is a plain `version =` change with no release-notes entry, no module migration, and no documentation update. The `services.opencloud` module also has no mechanism to reconcile an out-of-date `opencloud.yaml` because the only writer of that file is the `opencloud-init-config.service` oneshot, which is gated on the file not yet existing — `nixos/modules/services/web-apps/opencloud.nix:180-203`:

```nix
opencloud-init-config = lib.mkIf (cfg.settings.opencloud or { } == { }) {
  …
  script = ''
    config="''${OC_CONFIG_DIR}/opencloud.yaml"
    if [ ! -e "$config" ]; then
      echo "Provisioning initial OpenCloud config..."
      opencloud init --insecure "''${OC_INSECURE:false}" --config-path "''${OC_CONFIG_DIR}"
      chown ${cfg.user}:${cfg.group} "$config"
    fi
  '';
};
```

So on a host that was initialised pre-7.0, that script does nothing on subsequent boots and the `opencloud.yaml` is never migrated — every existing user hits this on the next `nixos-rebuild switch`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On any earlier nixpkgs rev, enable `services.opencloud` with the defaults documented in `nixos/modules/services/web-apps/opencloud.md`. Let it boot at least once so `opencloud init` writes `/etc/opencloud/opencloud.yaml`.
2. Update nixpkgs past #522661 (which brings opencloud to 7.0).
3. `sudo nixos-rebuild switch` → `opencloud.service` enters `failed` with the error above.

### Expected behaviour

`nixos-rebuild switch` to a 7.0 evaluation either:

- migrates the existing `opencloud.yaml` (e.g. copies an existing `service_account` block into `sharing:` from a sibling service — the same one-line migration `community-scripts/ProxmoxVE#14650` applies for their auto-upgrade), **or**
- the module documents the required manual step (set `SHARING_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID` / `SHARING_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_SECRET`, or declare it via `services.opencloud.settings.sharing.service_account`), **or**
- nixpkgs at least carries a release-notes entry pointing operators at the upstream upgrade guide: https://docs.opencloud.eu/docs/admin/maintenance/upgrade/upgrade-guide/#verify-configuration-changes

### Relevant log output

```console
opencloud[…]: The service account id has not been configured for sharing. Make sure your
              /etc/opencloud config contains the proper values …
systemd[1]: opencloud.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
systemd[1]: opencloud.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
systemd[1]: opencloud.service: Scheduled restart job, restart counter is at 5.
systemd[1]: opencloud.service: Start request repeated too quickly.
systemd[1]: opencloud.service: Failed with result 'start-limit-hit'.
systemd[1]: Failed to start OpenCloud …
```

### Workaround

Either of these unblock the host without touching `/etc/opencloud/opencloud.yaml`:

```nix
# 1. Declarative — uses the existing `settings` escape hatch.
#    Creates /etc/openclou

### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.05)

### Describe the bug

Themes are not packaged, since it does not use the HELIX_DEFAULT_RUNTIME directory.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build the package and use it
2. Set your theme: `:theme material_oceanic`

### Expected behaviour

I expected the themes to load

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Relevant log output

_No response_

### Additional context

To fix, make the build script more similar to the helix-unwrapped package. I've made an overlay that fixes this issue in the meantime:

```nix
    steelix = prev.steelix.overrideAttrs (oldAttrs: {
      outputs = prev.helix-unwrapped.outputs;
      postPatch = prev.helix-unwrapped.postPatch;
      postBuild = prev.helix-unwrapped.postBuild;
      postInstall = prev.helix-unwrapped.postInstall;
      nativeBuildInputs = prev.helix-unwrapped.nativeBuildInputs;

      env = {
        HELIX_DISABLE_AUTO_GRAMMAR_BUILD = "1";
        HELIX_DEFAULT_RUNTIME =
          let
            defaultRuntimeDir = final.runCommand "helix-default-runtime" { } ''
              cp -r --no-preserve=mode ${oldAttrs.src}/runtime $out
              rm -rf $out/grammars $out/queries
            '';

          in
          defaultRuntimeDir;
      };
    });
```

This will also fix the docs not being packaged. The helix package should be overridden to use this package for proper language support:

```nix
    helix = prev.helix.override {
      helix-unwrapped = final.steelix;
    };
```

### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.05)

### Describe the bug

Hi, I run into a problem trying to use netbird native ssh (https://docs.netbird.io/manage/peers/ssh#native-ssh-clients-open-ssh).

Netbird creates a file `/etc/ssh/ssh_config.d/99-netbird.conf`, but default openssh configuration under nixos doesn't include `/etc/ssh/ssh_config.d` directory, thus the file is never read.

From my perspective it'd be best to specifically include `/etc/ssh/ssh_config.d/99-netbird.conf` when services.netbird.clients.* is specified. I'd be happy to create a PR if this is the right approach.

### Steps to reproduce

1. enable netbird with services.netbird.clients.*
2. try to ssh into any netbird host
3. get password prompt and no jwt flow - ssh config not read

Netbird native ssh would work out of the box.

payload.author: PaulGrandperrin
payload.body:
This is the exact issue as described here: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/19809

This issue has been fixed in upstream systemd (actually in util-linux: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/17788#issuecomment-736942115) but the issue persists only on NixOS.

The cause is simple:
- systemd's mount unit's code hardcodes the path to the `umount` executable to `/usr/bin/umount` (https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/4d18eac5a99dbc8198f25cde9175e66f27e92cbc/meson.build#L623)
-  and nixpkgs overrides it to `${lib.getOutput "mount" util-linux}/bin/umount` (https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/nixos-unstable/pkgs/os-specific/linux/systemd/default.nix#L437).
- `/usr/bin/umount` is supposed to have the `suid` bit set but nix store path don't.

The solution: use `/run/wrappers/bin/umount`.

I'll post a corresponding PR.

payload.author: OCharnyshevich
payload.body:
### Describe the bug

`buildGoModule` infinite-recurses at evaluation time on `x86_64-freebsd`. Reproduces with a no-op call (no real source, no module deps), so it's not specific to any package being built. The chain runs through Go's `iana-etc` patch → `unzip` → `bzip2` → `autoreconf-hook` → `autoconf` → `texinfo` → `gettext` → `libc-iconv` → `libc` → `include` → `rpcgen` → `bmake` → `bmake-filtered-src` → `rsync`'s `buildInputs`, where it loops.

### Steps To Reproduce

```sh
nix eval --impure --expr '
  (import <nixpkgs> { system = "x86_64-freebsd"; }).buildGoModule {
    pname       = "x";
    version     = "0";
    src         = builtins.toFile "x" "";
    vendorHash  = null;
  }
'
# «error: infinite recursion encountered»
```

`hello` and `go` themselves evaluate cleanly on `x86_64-freebsd`, so it's not a generic stdenv break — it's specifically `buildGoModule`'s pull-in chain.

### Expected behavior

Derivation evaluates (it would fail at build time on a non-FreeBSD builder, but eval should not recurse).

### Stack trace (key frames)

```
… while evaluating derivation 'x-0'
  … attribute 'disallowedReferences'
… while evaluating derivation 'go-1.25.9'
  … attribute 'patches'
… while evaluating derivation 'iana-etc-1.25.patch'
  … attribute 'buildPhase'
… while evaluating derivation 'iana-etc-20250505'
  … attribute 'src' → 'source' (unzip-6.0 → bzip2-1.0.8 → autoreconf-hook
  → autoconf-2.72 → texinfo-7.2 → gettext-0.25.1 → libc-iconv-14.2.0
  → libc-14.2.0 → include-14.2.0 → rpcgen-14.2.0)
… while evaluating derivation 'bmake-14.2.0'
  … attribute 'src'
… while evaluating derivation 'bmake-filtered-src'
  … attribute 'nativeBuildInputs'
… while evaluating derivation 'rsync-3.4.1'
  … attribute 'buildInputs'

error: infinite recursion encountered
```

### Additional context

Reproduces on `nixos-unstable` HEAD as of 2026-05-23. Tested via both a flake-pinned commit (`d233902339c02a9c334e7e593de68855ad26c4cb`) and a fresh `fetchTarball` of `nixos-unstable`. #344131 (closed) is unrelated — that one was about `pkgsCross.x86_64-freebsd.hello` cross-evaluation; this is `legacyPackages.x86_64-freebsd` with `buildGoModule` and persists today.

Discovered while running `nix flake check --all-systems` on a Go-toolchain mirror flake. Workaround: gate any `buildGoModule`-using derivation on `!pkgs.stdenv.hostPlatform.isFreeBSD` — see https://github.com/openserbia/go-flake/blob/main/flake.nix (`sourceBuiltSupported`).

### Metadata

- system: `"x86_64-linux"` (eval host) targeting `"x86_64-freebsd"` via `legacyPackages`
- nix version: 2.31.5
- nixpkgs: `nixos-unstable`

### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.05)

### Describe the bug

When building with gcc.arch and gcc.tune set to "haswell", VirtualBox fails to build with the following error:

```
/build/VirtualBox-7.2.8/out/linux.amd64/release/obj/bin2c/bin2c: size=57921 - Not 32768-57344b in size!
```

### Steps to reproduce

`nix-build -E 'let pkgs = import <nixpkgs> { localSystem = { system = "x86_64-linux"; gcc.arch = "haswell"; gcc.tune = "haswell"; }; }; in pkgs.virtualbox'`

### Expected behaviour

Builds successfully.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Relevant log output

```console
kBuild: bin2c iPxeBiosBin - /build/VirtualBox-7.2.8/out/linux.amd64/release/obj/iPxeBiosBin/iPxeBiosBin.rom
/build/VirtualBox-7.2.8/out/linux.amd64/release/obj/bin2c/bin2c: size=57921 - Not 32768-57344b in size!
```

### Additional context

This happens because while VirtualBox sets `-march=i386` when building the iPxe rom, it does not set `-mtune`. Normally, `-mtune` would default to the same as `-march`, but since `-mtune` was previously set by the gcc wrapper, the previous value is kept. As such, gcc ends up compiling with `-march=i386 -mtune=haswell`, which generates code too large to fit in the iPxe region of the memory map.

Applying this patch fixes the build:

```diff
--- a/src/VBox/Devices/PC/ipxe/Makefile.kmk	2025-10-17 01:59:31.000000000 -0700
+++ b/src/VBox/Devices/PC/ipxe/Makefile.kmk	2026-05-20 18:22:52.131710173 -0700
@@ -125,6 +125,7 @@
 	-ffreestanding \
 	-ffunction-sections \
 	-march=i386 \
+	-mtune=i386 \
 	-fomit-frame-pointer \
 	-fstrength-reduce \
 	-falign-jumps=1 \
```

payload.body:
### Nixpkgs version

- Stable (25.11)

### Describe the bug

I am trying to use NixOS `boot.initrd.clevis` to auto-unlock a ZFS native-encrypted root pool with a TPM2-sealed Clevis JWE.

The system uses:

- systemd initrd
- ZFS native encryption for the root pool (`rpool`)
- Lanzaboote secure boot
- `boot.initrd.clevis`
- TPM2 sealing with Clevis
- PCRs including PCR4

The current NixOS ZFS/Clevis integration places the JWE in the initrd as `/etc/clevis/rpool.jwe`, then the generated ZFS import service runs roughly:

```sh
clevis decrypt < /etc/clevis/rpool.jwe | zfs load-key -L prompt rpool || true
```

This works for putting the JWE into the unlock path, but appears to conflict with PCR4 sealing.

If I seal the JWE against PCRs including PCR4, then include that JWE in the initrd, the JWE itself changes the initrd contents. 

Lanzaboote's measured boot documentation says PCR4 is the most important measurement because it covers the bootloader and Lanzaboote stub, and the stub verifies the hashes of the initrd, kernel, and cmdline. That makes sense, but it also seems to mean that a Clevis JWE embedded into the initrd becomes part of the boot state that PCR4 is intended to cover. 

This means the current NixOS `boot.initrd.clevis` ZFS integration appears incompatible with Lanzaboote's recommended PCR4 measured-boot policy when using Clevis' static TPM2 PCR sealing.

So the loop appears to be:

```
create rpool.jwe sealed to current PCR4
  -> include rpool.jwe in initrd
  -> initrd changes
  -> boot artifact / measured boot state changes
  -> PCR4 changes
  -> rpool.jwe no longer decrypts
```

I observed this in practice: after re-wrapping the JWE and rebuilding, the next boot still fell back to the passphrase prompt. Comparing PCR values showed PCR4 changed while the other selected PCRs stayed stable.

If I understand correctly, this is not a ZFS encryption failure and not a Lanzaboote secure boot failure. The issue is that the sealed blob is itself part of what PCR4 measures.

### Steps to reproduce


1. Configure a NixOS system with systemd initrd, Lanzaboote, and a ZFS native-encrypted root pool.

2. Enable ZFS credential prompting:

    ```nix
    boot.zfs.requestEncryptionCredentials = [ "rpool" ];
    ```

3. Enable Clevis for the root pool:
```
    boot.initrd.clevis = {
      enable = true;
      devices.rpool.secretFile = ./clevis/rpool.jwe;
    };
```
4. Create sealed/rpool.jwe by sealing the ZFS passphrase with Clevis against TPM2 PCRs including PCR4, for example:
```
    systemd-ask-password "rpool passphrase: " | tr -d '\n' \
      | clevis encrypt tpm2 \
          '{"pcr_ids":"0,1,2,3,4,7","pcr_bank":"sha256"}' \
      > clevis/rpool.jwe
```
5. Rebuild and install the bootloader.
6. Reboot.
7. Observe that automatic unlock fails and the system falls back to the ZFS passphrase prompt.
8. Compare PCR values before and after the rebuild/reboot cycle. In my case PCR4 changed while the other selected PCRs stayed stable.


### Expected behaviour

I am not sure what the correct NixOS abstraction should be, but I think the current limitation should either be documented or handled explicitly.

Expected behavior could be one of:

- (preferred) support a way for ZFS/Clevis initrd unlock to consume a sealed blob that is not itself embedded into the measured initrd artifact, or 
- document that `boot.initrd.clevis` embeds the JWE into the initrd and therefore is not suitable for static PCR4 sealing, or
- point users toward another supported integration for ZFS native encryption with TPM/PCR4 measured boot.


### Screenshots

_No response_

### Relevant log output

```console

```

### Additional context

Related material I found while investigating:

- Clevis TPM2 static PCR policy brittleness / authorized policies:
  https://github.com/latchset/clevis/issues/121

- OpenZFS discussion of `systemd-creds` / `LoadCredentialEncrypted=` with `zfs load-key -L file://$CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY/...`:
  https://github.com/openzfs/zfs/issues
